newsitem.title: GERMANY: Spar says aims to lift 97 sales 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Spar says aims to lift 97 sales 10 pct.

text.p: German retail group Spar Handels AG said on Tuesday it expected 1997 sales to rise about 10 percent after acquisitions boosted first-half revenue 13.1 percent to 6.88 billion marks ($3.7 billion).

The company also said first-half operating profit before minorities rose 21.2 percent to 49.8 million marks ($26.7 million), but expected demand in the grocery sector to remain soft for the rest of this year.

"The management board expects that also in the second half of 1997 there will be no economic improvement in grocery trade," Spar said in a letter to shareholders. "The Spar Handels AG expects therefore an increase of sales of 10 percent and a good net profit."

In the first six months of 1997, Spar saw "no positive impulse" in its core grocery business. Sales in the period were boosted by its May takeover of eight warehouse stores and one Cash & Carry outlet from Holzer-Parkauf GmbH.
The stores have sales volume of about 163 million marks, Spar said.
As part of a plan to focus on grocery stores, Spar in June sold four of its five remaining building supply outlets. The fifth would be used to expand an existing Interspar store.

Spar also said that at the end of June the European Commission approved the sale of 75 percent plus one share of Spar's common shares to Intercontessa AG. Intercontessa is 51 percent owned by Paris-based ITM Enterprise SA.
